description.comment: The common starling (Sturnus vulgaris), also known simply as the starling in Great Britain and Ireland, and as European starling in North America, is a medium-sized passerine bird in the starling family, Sturnidae. Its gift for mimicry has been noted in literature including the Mabinogion and the works of Pliny the Elder and William Shakespeare (from Wikipedia entry). This sample of a female individual was procured by Melanie Couture and Jean-Nicolas Audet at the Rockefeller University Field Research Center in Millbrook, New York, for a vocal learning study and to generate a high-quality reference genome for the Vertebrate Genomes Project (VGP). Sequencing and genome assembly were conducted at the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco.

assembly_info.comments: The Z and W chromosomes were identified and curated based on their synteny with a previously published genome and a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assembly of Taeniopygia guttata. For the curation of microchromosomes and dot chromosomes, the following approaches were applied:(1) MicroFinder was used to identify scaffolds containing genes typically found on avian microchromosomes. (2) A subsampled PretextMap was generated using scaffolds shorter than 10 Mb. (3) A synteny map was constructed using alignments against the Zebra Finch T2T genome. Several scaffolds of repetitive sequences that interact with micro, dot and W chromosomes were not possible to assign to chromosomes. These scaffolds were left unplaced. Scaffolds that were identified in the T2T alignment to match with dot chromosomes, but for which there was no clear order, were left as unloc, and the scaffolds with the larger size were used as the main scaffolds
